acceptance_criteria: AC-1 A movement with no usage cache file renders unknown in the turns, tokens and cache columns.
AC-2 A movement whose usage cache exists and recorded no events renders unknown in those three columns, not zero.
AC-3 A movement that genuinely measured a zero still renders 0, and a test distinguishes this case from AC-2.
AC-4 The metered and subscription totals, and the unavailable-cost count, are unchanged for every existing row.
AC-5 A human assessment cell still survives a re-render untouched.
AC-6 tests/test_dispatch_ledger.py and tests/test_orchestrator_usage.py pass with the new tests, and the repository privacy gate passes.

baseline.authority: docs/design/GOV_ORCH_13_THE_DISPATCH_LEDGER.md -- FROZEN, Product Owner directive 2026-09-14: DL-3 fixes the column set; DL-4 cost honesty, a subscription figure is a comparable and never billed spend, and an unavailable cost is counted in neither total; DL-5 the assessment column is human and the renderer never overwrites it; DL-6 derived, never authored -- duration comes from the record's own timestamps and an absent or negative value is printed as unknown rather than computed into a number. Supporting: GOV_ORCH_4A CU-4.
baseline.engineering_baseline: scripts/dispatch_ledger.py renders project/DISPATCH_LEDGER.md from the orchestrator's records; scripts/orchestrator_usage.py owns the per-movement usage cache and the summary the renderer reads. Sixty attempts are recorded today across three providers.
baseline.product_baseline: Not a product change. The Java product, its collectors and its UI are untouched.
baseline.test_baseline: tests/test_dispatch_ledger.py and tests/test_orchestrator_usage.py pass on origin/main today, run locally on 2026-09-15 before this packet was written.
baseline.what_exists:
The real committed row for the movement that exposed this reads exactly:

| NXS-LOCAL-0183 | 1 | 2026-09-14T21:19:35Z | antigravity | pro | unknown | unknown | 0 | 0 | 0.00% | unknown | unavailable | unknown | done | 336 | ... |

The columns, in order, are: movement, attempt, started, provider, model, effort, minutes, turns, tokens, cache %, cost, source, budget, outcome, PR, assessment. So turns, tokens and cache are the three cells printing a measured-looking zero for a movement whose usage was never measured at all.

scripts/orchestrator_usage.py::usage_summary_only returns a dict built like this, and the renderer reads those keys:

    return {
        "provider": provider,
        "turns": cache.get("turns", 0),
        "input_tokens": tokens["input_tokens"],
        "cache_creation_input_tokens": tokens["cache_creation_input_tokens"],
        "cache_read_input_tokens": tokens["cache_read_input_tokens"],
        "output_tokens": tokens["output_tokens"],
        "total_tokens": total_tokens,
        "uncached_input_tokens": tokens["input_tokens"],
        "cache_hit_ratio": cache_hit_ratio,
        "cost_usd": cost_usd,
        "cost_source": cost_source,
        "model": cache.get("model"),
        "last_event_at": cache.get("last_event_at"),
    }

and the cache-hit line just above it is:

    cache_hit_ratio = round(tokens["cache_read_input_tokens"] / denom, 4) if denom else 0.0

The usage cache file for a movement lives at <state_dir>/usage/<movement_id>.json; scripts/orchestrator_usage.py::_usage_path returns that path, and scripts/dispatch_ledger.py already calls _usage_path(...).is_file() to decide whether a row has usage at all.

invariants: Derived, never authored: no absent value is ever computed into a number.
The assessment column is human and is preserved on every re-render.
Metered and subscription figures never sum together.
The ledger holds movement identifiers and numbers only: no address, hostname, serial, credential or path to a credential.
report.merge_gate: Product Owner assistant review plus orchestrator verify.passed. The worker does not open a pull request and does not merge.
report.objective: Stop the dispatch ledger printing a zero where it has no measurement. A participant that emits no usage stream renders turns 0, tokens 0 and cache 0.00 percent. A zero claims nothing was spent; the truth is that nothing was measured, and GOV.ORCH.13 DL-6 says an absent value prints unknown and is never computed into a number.
output_contract: A ledger whose every number is something that was actually measured.

recommended_reasoning.reason: Two scripts and their tests; the defect, the real row and the exact summary shape are all pasted.

requirements: English, per AGENTS.md engineering-output language law.
Every command runs from the repository root.
Every changed function names the clause it implements (GOV.ORCH.13 DL-n).
Run only the commands named above.
Mechanical mismatches between this packet and the code are settled against the code and named in the SESSION_CLOSE; a RELAY_QUESTION is only for a decision in conflict.
No emoji, no tool-identifying footer, no external URL in commits, the pull request or code comments.
Commit early and often on your lane.
The SESSION_CLOSE names how absent is represented, where it is decided, and what proves a genuine zero still renders as zero.
risks: Collapsing absent and zero into one representation somewhere in the middle of the chain, which puts the defect back one layer down where no test looks.
Breaking an existing caller of the usage summary that reasonably expects a number.
Changing the totals by treating a newly-unknown cell as an unavailable cost, which would move the counts DL-4 fixes.

in: Distinguish an absent usage record from a recorded zero. A movement whose usage cache file does not exist, and a movement whose cache exists but recorded no events at all, both have no measurement; a movement that genuinely processed zero of something has one. Choose one representation for the absent case -- None is the obvious one -- and carry it through rather than substituting a number anywhere on the way.

scripts/dispatch_ledger.py: turns, tokens and cache render the literal word unknown when there is no measurement, exactly as minutes and cost already do. The cache percentage in particular must not print 0.00% for a movement that never reported a cache field.

scripts/orchestrator_usage.py: whatever change is needed so the absent case is expressible. Keep every existing caller working; a caller that expects a number today must keep getting one where a measurement exists.

tests: a movement with no usage cache renders unknown in turns, tokens and cache; a movement with a cache recording genuine zeros still renders 0; the totals and the unavailable-cost count are unchanged by either.
out: Estimating, inferring or back-filling any figure for a participant that reports nothing. An invented number is worse than an honest unknown and DL-6 forbids it.
Any change to the column set, their order, or their headings.
Any change to the assessment column's preservation. DL-5 is not touched by this movement and a re-render must still keep every human cell exactly.
Any change to how cost or cost_source is computed, or to the separation of metered and subscription totals.
Re-rendering project/DISPATCH_LEDGER.md with real numbers. Leave the committed ledger alone; the Product Owner renders it from the main checkout.
